documents.title: Northwind Cloud AI Engineer Associate certification guide
documents.text:
The Northwind Cloud AI Engineer Associate certification validates that a candidate can design, build and deploy machine learning solutions on Northwind Cloud.

Exam format: 50 multiple-choice and case-study questions, 120 minutes, delivered online with a remote proctor. The passing score is 700 on a scale of 1000.

Exam fee: the registration fee is 165 US dollars per attempt. Retakes are charged at the full fee after a 14-day waiting period.

Prerequisites: there is no mandatory prior certification, but candidates should have at least one year of hands-on Python experience and should be comfortable with REST APIs. Northwind recommends completing its free Intro to Machine Learning path first.

Validity: the certification is valid for two years. Renewal requires passing a free online renewal assessment.

documents.title: Applied ML Practitioner Certificate - Lumen Institute
documents.text:
The Applied ML Practitioner Certificate from the Lumen Institute is a project-based credential for working engineers who want to apply machine learning in production.

How it works: instead of a timed exam, learners submit three graded capstone projects over twelve weeks: a tabular prediction model, a text classification service and a monitoring dashboard. Mentors review each project.

Cost: the programme costs 300 US dollars, which includes mentor reviews. Financial aid is available on application.

Prerequisites: there are no formal prerequisites. A working knowledge of statistics and one programming language is strongly recommended.

The Lumen Institute does not publish an expiry date for the certificate.

documents.title: Foundations of Prompt Engineering (OpenLearn Commons)
documents.text:
Foundations of Prompt Engineering is a free, self-paced online course from OpenLearn Commons.

Duration: six weeks at roughly three hours per week. Each week combines short videos, readings and a hands-on lab in a notebook environment.

Topics: how large language models work at a high level, writing clear instructions, few-shot examples, structured outputs, evaluation of prompts, and an introduction to retrieval-augmented generation.

Prerequisites: basic programming in any language. No machine learning background is required.

All course material is free to audit. An optional verified certificate of completion costs 49 US dollars.

documents.title: Chunk small: why short passages win for retrieval
documents.text:
When building retrieval-augmented generation systems, we found that small chunks of about 200 to 300 tokens consistently gave the best results.

Short passages make embeddings more specific. A long chunk mixes several topics, so its vector ends up as a blurry average and matches many queries weakly. With small chunks, the retriever returns exactly the sentences that answer the question.

In our tests, moving from 1,000-token chunks to 256-token chunks improved retrieval precision noticeably and reduced the amount of irrelevant text sent to the model.

Our recommendation: start with roughly 256 tokens per chunk and a small overlap of about 10 percent.

documents.title: Bigger chunks, better answers
documents.text:
A popular tip says retrieval systems should split documents into tiny pieces. In our experience that advice hurts answer quality.

Tiny chunks strip away the surrounding context. The model receives isolated sentences, loses track of definitions introduced a paragraph earlier and produces confident but incomplete answers.

We recommend chunks of 800 to 1,000 tokens. Larger passages keep arguments and their caveats together, and modern embedding models handle longer inputs well.

If precision is a concern, add a reranking step rather than shrinking chunks below 500 tokens.

documents.title: Keeping a sourdough starter alive
documents.text:
A sourdough starter is a culture of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria that leavens bread.

Feed the starter once a day at room temperature with equal weights of flour and water after discarding about half of it. In the fridge, weekly feeding is enough.

A healthy starter roughly doubles within four to eight hours after feeding and smells pleasantly sour. A layer of grey liquid on top means it is hungry: pour it off and feed it.

documents.title: Study notes: vector databases
documents.text:
Vector databases store embeddings and support nearest-neighbour search. Common index types are HNSW, which builds a navigable graph, and IVF, which clusters vectors into lists.

Cosine similarity is the usual metric for normalised text embeddings.
